# lcd.drawMask

<div class="api-badges"><span class="api-badge api-badge--since">since 1.1.0</span></div>

Draw a mask.

```lua
lcd.drawMask(x, y, mask)
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | yes | X coordinate |
| `y` | number | yes | Y coordinate |
| `mask` | Mask | yes | mask |

## Returns

Nothing.

## Examples

```lua
local ARROW = lcd.loadMask("gfx/arrow.png")   -- file level

local function paint(widget)
  lcd.color(lcd.RGB(255, 200, 0))   -- the mask is painted in the current color
  lcd.drawMask(10, 10, ARROW)
end
```

Masks are single-channel images, cheaper than full-color bitmaps and recolorable, so they suit icons that should follow the theme or signal state with color.

<div class="api-usage">Called 2 times across 2 open-source Ethos Lua projects. A few short excerpts:</div>

=== "Example 1"

    ```lua
    local minIconY = labelY + (labelH or 0) + iconGap
    local iconY = by + bh - iconSize - iconBottomPad
    if iconY < minIconY then iconY = minIconY end
    lcd.drawMask(math.floor(bx + (bw - iconSize) / 2 + 0.5), math.floor(iconY + 0.5), mask)
    ```
